note: Sali molecolari di metformina (MTF) con cinque FANS (MEF, TLF, NIF, DIF, FLP). I CCDC 2232928-2232933 sono dati come intervallo senza attribuzione alle sei strutture della Table 2 (MTF–MEF, MTF–TLF, MTF–NIF, MTF–NIF·2H2O, MTF–DIF, MTF–FLP): restano qui. Incoerenze dell'articolo: (1) il testo dice 'MTF–TLF increased solubility 111 times, MTF–MEF 208 times, MTF–NIF·2H2O 574 times, and finally MTF–FLP 1110 times' ma la Table 3 da' MEF 119x e TLF 208x (e 0.0127x/0.0110x per MTF); (2) aging: i Metodi dicono 'for two months', i Risultati 'after four months'; (3) il flurbiprofene e' 'FLF' nell'introduzione e 'FLP' dopo; (4) intestazioni della Table 2 'MFT–' invece di 'MTF–'; (5) la didascalia della Figure 7(c) parla di 'NIF anions' e 'MTF–DIF' per la struttura di MTF–FLP; (6) 'Metfomin·HCl' nei Metodi; (7) la frase 'ranging from 250 mg/mL [46,62,63]' sulla solubilita' di MTF·HCl e' troncata e non e' stata estratta; (8) per MTF–NIF il testo dice sia 'an intermediate phase or a hydrate phase' sia, nei Metodi, 'hydrates'. Non estratti: i punti di fusione dei coformeri (MEF 230, DIF 210–211, TLF 207, NIF 204 °C; FLP 110 °C implicito) perche' dati senza riferimento e senza dire quale forma (sono usati solo come estremi degli intervalli di fusione dei sali); la degradazione dopo la fusione ('other endothermic events ... ascribed to the degradation') senza temperatura; i fattori di miglioramento di solubilita' e i ΔpKa, che sono derivati. citazioni: MTF–MEF was obtained by LAG of a mixture of MTF (0.5 mmol, 64.58 mg) and MEF (0.5 mmol, 120.64 mg) in a 1:1 stoichiometric ratio with 100 µL of ultrapure water as a liquid additive.

The mechanochemical synthesis of MTF salts was conducted using Liquid-Assisted Grinding (LAG) in a Retsh MM2000 ball mill (Retsch, Haan, Germany), operating at a 25-Hz frequency, using stainless steel jars along with stainless steel balls 7 mm in diameter.
All reaction syntheses lasted for 30 min and were repeated to ensure reproducibility.

In this work, LAG reactions were performed using a 1:1 stoichiometric mixture of metformin base, previously neutralized, and the corresponding NSAIDs, along with ultrapure water or ethanol as an additive solvent. After 30 min of reaction, the powder obtained in each reaction was characterized using PXRD and compared with the corresponding parent APIs to evaluate the formation of the new salts. PXRD patterns demonstrated the formation of five new phases after LAG reactions and their purity (Figure 1 and Figure S1).

The structural information allowed the simulation of a calculated PXRD for each salt (Figure S1), which confirmed the phase purity of the bulk products obtained from LAG except for MTF–NIF, whose calculated powder pattern did not match the product obtained from the LAG reaction, thus indicating the formation of an intermediate phase or a hydrate phase.
eventi.note: MTF base + MEF 1:1 con 100 µL di acqua ultrapura: il prodotto del LAG e' il sale MTF–MEF (fase pura secondo il confronto col PXRD calcolato). Quantita' dei reagenti: 0.5 mmol di ciascuno (64.58 e 120.64 mg). Il rapporto liquido/solido (η) non e' dato nel testo.

gruppi_coinvolti.citazione: SCXRD data confirmed the proton transfer from the acid groups of NSAIDs to the basic nitrogen site of metformin.
SCXRD data confirmed the proton transfer from the acid groups of NSAIDs to the basic nitrogen site of metformin.

Due to the protonation of MTF, the resulting MTF+ cation is able to participate in hetero-synthons with the NSAID anion through guanidinium···carboxylate synthons, engaged through the R228 ring motif [54,55].
The disruption of the robust NSAID–NSAID dimers present in the crystal structure of isolated NSAIDs is key for understanding their enhancement in solubility.

condizioni.rapporto_solido_solvente: An excess of powder samples of each phase was added to 1 mL of buffer phosphate (pH 6.8)

citazioni: Stability in an aqueous solution was evaluated through slurry experiments. An excess of powder samples of each phase was added to 1 mL of buffer phosphate (pH 6.8) and stirred for 24 h in sealed vials. The solids were collected, filtered, dried, and analyzed with PXRD.

The thermodynamic stability of molecular salts was studied by conducting aqueous slurry experiments at 25 °C. After 24 h, the suspensions were filtered, air-dried at room temperature, and characterized using PXRD (Figure S4).

Despite MTF–NIF and MTF–DIF displaying a phase transition indicating low stability in solution, MTF–TLF, MTF–MEF, and MTF–FLP remained stable upon slurrying, as the crystallinity and the initial crystal structures remained intact.
SCXRD and further PXRD confirmed the formation of the dihydrate salt of MTF–NIF, but it was impossible to determine the final phase of MTF–DIF.
A phase transformation for MTF–NIF was confirmed through the obtention of MTF–NIF·2H2O single crystals.

In the case of MTF–NIF, the faces {−110}, {−1–10}, {1 1 0} and {1 −1 0} (corresponding to 14.4 % of the total surface) and the faces {1 −1 −1}, {1 1 −1}, {−1 −1 1} and {−1 1 1} (corresponding to 32 % of the total surface) expose amino groups of MTF and carboxylate groups of NIF to the surface and coincide with the crystal structure region where the ion pairs form the tape-like structures. Therefore, it seems reasonable that water molecules can access and form additional H-bonds with the groups involved resulting in the hydrated structure as reported herein.
eventi.note: MTF–NIF (anidro) in sospensione in tampone fosfato a pH 6.8 a 25 °C per 24 h diventa il diidrato MTF–NIF·2H2O (confermato da SCXRD e PXRD). Gli autori spiegano la trasformazione con la morfologia BFDH prevista: le facce espongono i gruppi amminici di MTF e carbossilati di NIF dove si formano le strutture a nastro, e l'acqua puo' fare legami H aggiuntivi (spiegazione dichiarata come 'possible', cioe' ipotesi). Il testo dei risultati dice solo 'aqueous slurry experiments at 25 °C'; il tampone pH 6.8 e' nei Metodi.

condizioni.rapporto_solido_solvente: An excess of powder samples of each phase was added to 1 mL of buffer phosphate (pH 6.8)

citazioni: Stability in an aqueous solution was evaluated through slurry experiments. An excess of powder samples of each phase was added to 1 mL of buffer phosphate (pH 6.8) and stirred for 24 h in sealed vials. The solids were collected, filtered, dried, and analyzed with PXRD.

The thermodynamic stability of molecular salts was studied by conducting aqueous slurry experiments at 25 °C. After 24 h, the suspensions were filtered, air-dried at room temperature, and characterized using PXRD (Figure S4).

Despite MTF–NIF and MTF–DIF displaying a phase transition indicating low stability in solution, MTF–TLF, MTF–MEF, and MTF–FLP remained stable upon slurrying, as the crystallinity and the initial crystal structures remained intact.
SCXRD and further PXRD confirmed the formation of the dihydrate salt of MTF–NIF, but it was impossible to determine the final phase of MTF–DIF.

Interestingly, this unknown phase agrees with the phase obtained directly from the LAG reaction using water as a liquid additive (Figure S5), suggesting the formation of a hydrate form of MTF–DIF salt.
On the other hand, the phase transformation for MTF–DIF could not be determined, thus, making MTF–DIF unsuitable for solubility studies.
eventi.note: MTF–DIF in sospensione cambia fase ('displaying a phase transition indicating low stability in solution'). La fase finale non e' stata determinata ('it was impossible to determine the final phase of MTF–DIF'), ma 'this unknown phase agrees with the phase obtained directly from the LAG reaction using water' (F8, idrato suggerito): a = F8 per identificazione con un altro esperimento, certezza media.

condizioni.rapporto_solido_solvente: An excess of powder samples of each phase was added to 1 mL of buffer phosphate (pH 6.8)

citazioni: Stability in an aqueous solution was evaluated through slurry experiments. An excess of powder samples of each phase was added to 1 mL of buffer phosphate (pH 6.8) and stirred for 24 h in sealed vials. The solids were collected, filtered, dried, and analyzed with PXRD.

The thermodynamic stability of molecular salts was studied by conducting aqueous slurry experiments at 25 °C. After 24 h, the suspensions were filtered, air-dried at room temperature, and characterized using PXRD (Figure S4).

Despite MTF–NIF and MTF–DIF displaying a phase transition indicating low stability in solution, MTF–TLF, MTF–MEF, and MTF–FLP remained stable upon slurrying, as the crystallinity and the initial crystal structures remained intact.
Saturated solutions were obtained by stirring an excess amount of APIs in 10 mL of pH 6.8 phosphate buffer at 25 °C until the thermodynamic equilibrium was reached after 24 h.
The remaining solids were finally analyzed using PXRD to identify the crystalline phases, thus confirming the stability of the initial phases and the congruent solubility of these new salts.
eventi.note: MTF–MEF resta stabile in sospensione in tampone pH 6.8 a 25 °C per 24 h ('remained stable upon slurrying, as the crystallinity and the initial crystal structures remained intact'). Frase che elenca tre sali: un evento per sale, certezza media. Anche nella prova di solubilita' (10 mL di tampone pH 6.8, 25 °C, 24 h) i solidi residui confermano 'the stability of the initial phases'.

osservazioni.cinetica: transizione parziale al terzo giorno, conversione finale a una settimana

citazioni: Stability at accelerated aging conditions was also studied: 200 mg of solid was placed in watch glasses and left at 40 °C in 75% relative humidity using a Memmert HPP110 climate chamber (Memmert, Schwabach, Germany). Under the above-accelerated aging conditions, the stability of the solid forms was periodically monitored using PXRD for two months.

The molecular salts were also stored under accelerated aging conditions (40 °C and 75% RH). Under these conditions, all the samples remained stable after four months, with the exception of MTF–NIF (Figure S6), which presented a partial phase transition on the third day, with a final conversion at one week.
This new phase matched neither the already determined dihydrate salt form nor the product of the LAG in water, suggesting the formation of different grades of hydrate salt for the MTF–NIF system.
eventi.note: MTF–NIF (anidro) a 40 °C e 75% RH: 'a partial phase transition on the third day, with a final conversion at one week'. Un solo evento (esito avvenuta, tempo di conversione una settimana); il parziale al terzo giorno e' nella cinetica. Prodotto F9, fase nuova che non e' il diidrato ne' il prodotto del LAG in acqua; idrato solo suggerito, quindi via 'umidita' / 'assorbimento' con certezza media. Il testo dice 'The molecular salts were also stored' (200 mg di solido in vetrini da orologio).

citazioni: Interestingly, the melting point of MTF–FLP is 200 °C, while the melting point of the components goes from 110 to 117 °C, increasing the thermal stability and the melting point of both APIs by more than 80 °C.

Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was used to evaluate the thermal stability and determine the melting point of the new phases. Figure 8 shows the DSC traces and the endothermic events occurring during the experiments, which correspond to the melting point of the salts.
Experimental conditions: aluminum crucibles of 40 µL volume, an atmosphere of dry nitrogen with 50 mL/min flow rate, and heating rates of 1 °C/min and 10 °C/min.
eventi.note: Fusione di MTF–FLP, 'the melting point of MTF–FLP is 200 °C' (unico sale a fondere sopra il coformero: 'while the melting point of the components goes from 110 to 117 °C'). Il testo non dice se e' onset o picco. Velocita' di riscaldamento 1 e 10 °C/min date per l'insieme delle prove DSC, non per sale. Crogioli di alluminio da 40 µL, tipo di coperchio non detto.

citazioni: With the exception of MTF–FLP, all the molecular salts show a melting point in a range between the melting point of the MTF base (117 °C) and the corresponding NSAID coformer (MEF 230 °C, DIF 210–211 °C, TLF 207 °C, NIF 204 °C), increasing the thermal stability of the MTF base in all cases, although still under the melting point of the commercially available MTF·HCl (231.5 °C) [46].

citazioni: All APIs and solvents used in this work were purchased from commercial sources and used as received.
preparazioni.note: Metformin·HCl, acido tolfenamico, acido niflumico e flurbiprofene da TCI Europe; diflunisal e acido mefenamico da Sigma-Aldrich.

citazioni: To obtain the MTF base, MTF·HCl was neutralized by stirring 10 mmol of MTF·HCl (1.656 g) and 10 mmol of NaOH (0.4 g) in 60 mL of isopropanol at room temperature, using a magnetic stirrer and a sealed glass beaker to avoid evaporation. After 24 h, the solution was filtered using 0.22 µm syringe filters to remove the NaCl (insoluble in isopropanol). The solvent of the clear filtered obtained (containing the MTF base) was removed using a rotatory evaporator set at 50 °C and 30 rpm. The remaining powder was dried and characterized by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) to confirm the purity of the MTF base obtained.
preparazioni.note: Neutralizzazione di MTF·HCl (F16) con NaOH in isopropanolo a temperatura ambiente, poi evaporazione del solvente al rotavapor a 50 °C e 30 rpm; reazione in soluzione, non un evento solido-solido.

citazioni: In this work, LAG reactions were performed using a 1:1 stoichiometric mixture of metformin base, previously neutralized, and the corresponding NSAIDs, along with ultrapure water or ethanol as an additive solvent. After 30 min of reaction, the powder obtained in each reaction was characterized using PXRD and compared with the corresponding parent APIs to evaluate the formation of the new salts. PXRD patterns demonstrated the formation of five new phases after LAG reactions and their purity (Figure 1 and Figure S1).

For that reason, the product of the LAG of MTF and NIF was heated at 100 °C for 2 h. After the thermal treatment, the PXRD pattern was in good agreement with the calculated powder pattern for MTF–NIF anhydrate salt.
preparazioni.note: Anidro MTF–NIF per disidratazione a 100 °C del prodotto di LAG (vedi evento).

citazioni: To obtain MTF–DIF and MTF–NIF as anhydrated salts, the product of the mechanochemical synthesis was heated at 100 °C for 2 h.

Although good-quality single crystals were obtained from hydrothermal reactions, the bulk material obtained from LAG did not match the PXRD pattern of the anhydride phase. Following the previous methodology, the product of the LAG was heated at 100 °C for 2 h. After the treatment, the PXRD patterns matched perfectly.
preparazioni.note: Anidro MTF–DIF per disidratazione a 100 °C del prodotto di LAG (vedi evento).

citazioni: Single crystals of MTF–based salts were obtained by dissolving the product of the LAGs in ethanol (for MTF–NIF·2H2O, MTF–MEF, MTF–FLP, and MTF–TLF) and ethyl acetate (for MTF–NIF).
After slow solvent evaporation at room temperature, suitable crystals for single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD) were obtained.
preparazioni.note: Cristalli singoli per SCXRD dal prodotto di LAG sciolto in etanolo e fatto evaporare lentamente a temperatura ambiente. Per MTF–NIF·2H2O il solido di partenza e' il prodotto di LAG idrato (F7).

preparazioni.rapporto_solido_solvente: 0.2 mmol of MTF (25.8 mg) and 0.2 mmol of DIF (50.4 mg) ... 3 mL of distilled water
citazioni: MTF–DIF single crystals were obtained using a hydrothermal reaction by placing a mixture of 0.2 mmol of MTF (25.8 mg) and 0.2 mmol of DIF (50.4 mg) in a hydrothermal reactor along with 3 mL of distilled water. The reactor was sealed and heated at 110 °C for 24 h. After cooling down to room temperature, the reactor was opened, and single crystals were separated from the solution for further characterization.
preparazioni.note: Sintesi idrotermale in reattore sigillato (cristalli singoli di MTF–DIF).
